title: Amazon ECS
description: Deploy and manage containers at scale using Amazon ECS clusters, task definitions, services, and Fargate.

data.text: Amazon Elastic Container Service (ECS) is AWS's native container orchestration service. It lets you run containers on a cluster of EC2 instances or on AWS Fargate, a serverless compute engine for containers.

An ECS cluster is a logical grouping of tasks or services. A task definition is a blueprint that describes your container: the Docker image, CPU and memory requirements, environment variables, ports, and logging configuration.

data.title: Task Definition Key Fields
items: **Container image** — the Docker image to run
**CPU / Memory** — resources reserved for the container
**Port mappings** — host port to container port
**Environment variables** — configuration passed to the container
**Log configuration** — where container logs are sent (CloudWatch, FireLens)

data.text: A task is an instantiation of a task definition running on a cluster. A service maintains a desired count of tasks and replaces any that fail or stop. Services can be connected to a load balancer to distribute traffic across tasks.

AWS Fargate removes the need to manage EC2 instances. You just specify the task definition and Fargate runs it. Fargate handles provisioning, scaling, and patching automatically. ECS Auto Scaling adjusts the number of tasks based on CPU, memory, or custom CloudWatch metrics.

Capacity providers manage the infrastructure for your tasks. The FARGATE and FARGATE_SPOT capacity providers let you run tasks on Fargate, while EC2 capacity providers let you run on self-managed EC2 instances. You can mix them for cost optimization.

terms.definition: A logical grouping of ECS tasks and services running on infrastructure.
A blueprint that describes how to run a container, including image, CPU, memory, and networking.
A long-running process that maintains a desired count of tasks and integrates with a load balancer.
A serverless compute engine for containers that removes the need to manage EC2 instances.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: ECS clusters group tasks; task definitions describe containers
Services maintain desired task counts and integrate with load balancers
Fargate runs containers without managing EC2 instances
Auto Scaling adjusts task counts based on demand
data.takeaway: ECS is AWS's managed container orchestration. Fargate makes it serverless — you define what to run, not where to run it.
